one-eye.name: The single eye
one-eye.blurb: A giant with one eye, and the blinding or losing of it. The motif recurs on separate continents with no plausible line of transmission between them.

body-cosmogony.name: A world built from a body
body-cosmogony.blurb: The earth, sky and sea are made from the dismembered corpse of a primordial giant. Mountains are bones; rivers are blood.

flood-survivor.name: Survivor of the flood
flood-survivor.blurb: A giant or giant-descended line survives a deluge that destroys the rest of its kind, and so carries the old world into the new one.

petrified.name: Turned to stone
petrified.blurb: A giant becomes a rock, hill or island. The landscape is offered as the surviving evidence, which is what makes the story durable.

builder.name: The giant as builder
builder.blurb: Walls, causeways, dolmens and bridges attributed to giants — usually structures whose real makers had been forgotten.

cannibal.name: Eater of people
cannibal.blurb: The giant as appetite: it takes travellers, children or the sick. Frequently a warning attached to a specific dangerous place.

pre-people.name: The people who came before
pre-people.blurb: Giants as an earlier race displaced by the present one. Often a way of accounting for ruins, large bones, or an older population.

outwitted.name: Defeated by cunning
outwitted.blurb: The giant loses to intelligence rather than strength — a trick, a false name, a riddle. Size is set up precisely so that it can fail.

sky-bearer.name: Holding up the sky
sky-bearer.blurb: A giant who carries or props the heavens, explaining why the sky stays where it is.

buried-sleeper.name: Sleeping under the land
buried-sleeper.blurb: The giant is not dead but sleeping beneath a mountain or island, and may yet wake. Ties a named place to an unfinished story.

wild-highland.name: The wild one of the uplands
wild-highland.blurb: A hairy, solitary giant of forest or mountain, hostile to herders and travellers — the shape a frontier takes in story.

colonial-distortion.name: Flattened by outsiders
colonial-distortion.blurb: A being from a living tradition rewritten by colonial-era writers into a simpler 'giant'. The distortion is itself part of the record.

war-on-heaven.name: War against the gods
war-on-heaven.blurb: Giants rise against the ruling powers and lose. The defeat is usually the point: it explains why the present order is the order.

eternal-punishment.name: Punished without end
eternal-punishment.blurb: Bound, stretched, buried or fed upon forever. The giant becomes a fixed feature of the cosmos rather than a character in it.

strength-from-earth.name: Strength drawn from the ground
strength-from-earth.blurb: The giant is unbeatable while touching its own soil, and is beaten by being lifted from it. Power is local, and that is the lesson.

many-limbed.name: Excess of body
many-limbed.blurb: Extra arms, heads, hands or fingers. Surplus anatomy marks a being as belonging to an older, less regulated order of creation.

star-become.name: Set among the stars
star-become.blurb: The dead giant is placed in the sky as a constellation, which keeps the story visible every clear night.

made-not-born.name: Made, not born
made-not-born.blurb: A giant forged rather than fathered — bronze, clay or craft. It raises the question of whether the thing is alive at all.

boon-abused.name: The gift that undoes
boon-abused.blurb: Devotion earns a boon; the boon is worded too cleverly and becomes the exact shape of the giant's destruction.

pious-adversary.name: The devout enemy
pious-adversary.blurb: An opponent of the gods who is also learned, generous or genuinely devoted. The tradition refuses to make him simply wicked.

guardian.name: The giant as guardian
guardian.blurb: Set to watch a place, an island or a people. Menace pointed outward instead of inward.

sun-chaser.name: Pursuing the sun
sun-chaser.blurb: A giant who races, shoots at or swallows the sun, and generally does not survive the attempt.

bones-as-proof.name: Bones offered as evidence
bones-as-proof.blurb: Large remains — real fossils, misread burials, or claims that no one can now examine — put forward to prove the giants were literal.

modern-rumour.name: Rumour of our own time
modern-rumour.blurb: A giant reported in living memory, circulating through soldiers, forums and video. Unverified by definition, and revealing regardless.

tall-tale.name: Knowingly tall tale
tall-tale.blurb: Exaggeration that never asked to be believed. The audience and the teller are both in on it, which makes it a different kind of story.

seasonal-visitor.name: Comes with the season
seasonal-visitor.blurb: A giant tied to a date in the calendar — midwinter, harvest, a feast — who arrives, is fed or feared, and leaves.

landscape-body.name: The land is the body
landscape-body.blurb: A named hill, lake or island is understood as a being, not merely as its memorial. The country is read as a person.
